notes: Provider-neutral suite for A/B-ing the Grok plugin against the Codex plugin it was retargeted from. Every assertion here is about outcomes both plugins claim to deliver — delegation reaches the CLI, the forwarder stays thin, the fix lands, the output reaches the user, review keeps its hands off the code. Provider-specific flag names are deliberately absent; those live in evals.json. Placeholders {{RESCUE_AGENT}} and {{PROGRESS_MARKER}} are substituted per provider.

evals.name: Delegation reaches the CLI and the fix actually lands
evals.prompt: the ttl test in test/cache.test.mjs is failing and i can't spot why. get {{PROVIDER}} to fix it
evals.expected_output: The rescue subagent is spawned, forwards once to the CLI, the bug is fixed, and the CLI's output is relayed to the user.

assertions.text: Spawns the rescue subagent instead of handling it in the main thread
The CLI run starts instead of dying on a rejected flag
assertions.pattern: refusing to start|could not apply the '|unknown model id|unrecognized|invalid value

assertions.text: Rescue subagent uses at most one tool call, and only Bash
Rescue subagent never reads, greps, or edits the repository itself
The outcome of the CLI run reaches the user (what changed and where)
The failing TTL test passes afterwards

evals.name: Review surfaces the defect and changes nothing
evals.expected_output: The CLI reviews the uncommitted change, the findings reach the user, and no file is touched.

assertions.text: The CLI run starts instead of dying on a rejected flag
assertions.pattern: refusing to start|could not apply the '|unknown model id|unrecognized|invalid value

assertions.text: Claude never invokes a file-editing tool during or after the review
Leaves every file in the repository untouched
The review identifies the TTL/expiresAt defect
Those findings appear in the user-visible response, not just the tool result

evals.name: Review does not start editing without being asked
evals.followup: which of those would you say is the most urgent?
evals.expected_output: A follow-up question about the findings grants no permission to edit. The plugin should answer and still leave the tree untouched.

assertions.text: Answers a follow-up question without editing anything
The review findings reached the user before any fix discussion

evals.name: Trivial local edits are not handed off
evals.prompt: add a short JSDoc comment above the get() method in src/cache.js explaining what it returns
evals.expected_output: Claude does this itself. The CLI is never invoked and the rescue subagent is never spawned.

assertions.text: Never invokes the delegated CLI for a task the main thread can finish
